response.rationale: The biopsy findings of coagulative necrosis with karyorrhexis and lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, along with tender lymphadenopathy and fever, are classic for Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.

rejected.why: Lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate and lymphadenopathy are nonspecific; lacks the characteristic karyorrhectic necrosis and clinical context of Kikuchi disease.
Normal laboratory studies and lack of non-caseating granulomas or other systemic features make sarcoidosis unlikely.
Rosai-Dorfman typically shows emperipolesis and fibrosis, not coagulative necrosis with karyorrhexis; less specific support.
